Case fractions are processed in ascending retained case index; cases with no contributing answers are omitted. Paired differences d use x=(d+1)/2 and return 2*bound-1. Brier differences use the same bounded mapping.

The predictable bet uses prior residual sum initialized at 0.25, pseudo-total 0.5, and t=count+1. variance=residual/t; bet=min(0.9, sqrt(2*log(1/alpha)/(variance*t*log(t+1)))). After the capital increment, total and count update, mu=total/(count+1), then residual+=(value-mu)^2. This is the implemented pseudo-observation residual convention.

Rejection uses the running maximum log capital >= log(1/alpha). Inversion uses an integer grid from 0 to 1000 divided by 1000; bounds retain the rejection boundary grid cell, giving outward rounding. One-sided bounds allocate alpha=0.05 to each requested tail. Two-sided 99% bounds allocate alpha=0.005 per tail. Empty answer cases are omitted before inversion. The fallback branch is opt-in: r0 widens with all-correct/any-correct case CP bounds, and difference_interval widens with its Hoeffding radius. Stage 17 calls the default fallback=False; no newly computed Stage 17 interval uses fallback.
